shorts3 = | socks3 = | current = 2026–27 Bayer 04 Leverkusen season }} '''Bayer 04 Leverkusen''', officially known as '''Bayer 04 Leverkusen Fußball GmbH''' ({{IPA|de|ˌbaɪ̯ɐ ˈleːvɐˌkuːzn̩|lang}}) and commonly known as '''Bayer Leverkusen''' or simply '''Leverkusen''', is a German professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Leverkusen]], [[North Rhine-Westphalia]].{{cite web |title=Sports – moving moments |url=http://www.nrwinvest.com/NRW_at_a_glance/Facts_Figures/Sports/index.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141015161207/http://www.nrwinvest.com/NRW_at_a_glance/Facts_Figures/Sports/index.php |archive-date=15 October 2014 |access-date=9 October 2014 |work=NRW Invest}} It competes in the [[Bundesliga]], the top tier of [[German football league system|German football]], and plays its home matches at the [[BayArena]].{{cite web |url=http://www.bundesliga.com/en/liga/clubs/bayer-leverkusen/daten.php |title=Bayer 04 Leverkusen – Club Data |website=bundesliga.com |publisher=Deutsche Fußball Liga |access-date=9 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141013103620/http://www.bundesliga.com/en/liga/clubs/bayer-leverkusen/daten.php |archive-date=13 October 2014 |url-status=dead }} Founded in 1904 by employees of the paint factory, today better known as a pharmaceutical company [[Bayer]] (whose headquarters are in Leverkusen and from which the club draws its name), the club was formerly a department of TSV Bayer 04 Leverkusen [[sports club]] whose members participate in athletics, gymnastics, [[Bayer Giants Leverkusen|basketball]], field and handball. In 1999, the football department was separated from the sports club. Bayer Leverkusen's main colours are red and black, which feature across their playing kits and badge, and their main rival is [[1. FC Köln]],{{cite web |url=http://www.bayer04.de/B04-ENG/en/_md_aktuell-dt.aspx?aktuell=aktuell-5267 |title=FC Köln derby a Saturday fixture |work=Bayer Leverkusen |date=25 September 2014 |access-date=9 October 2014 |archive-date=28 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220228144836/https://www.bayer04.de/B04-ENG/en/_md_aktuell-dt.aspx?aktuell=aktuell-5267 |url-status=live }} while the fans have had a deep friendship with the supporters of [[Kickers Offenbach]] for almost 50 years.{{Cite web |title=#BayerundderOFC – Friendly for a good cause |url=https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/news/bayer04/bayerundderofc-friendly-for-a-good-cause |access-date=11 August 2025 |website=Bayer 04 Leverkusen Fussball GmbH |language=en}} Bayer Leverkusen were promoted to the Bundesliga in [[1978–79 2. Bundesliga|1979]] and won their maiden top-flight honor, the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]], in [[1987–88 UEFA Cup|1988]]. The club won its first domestic honour, the [[DFB Pokal]], in [[1992–93 DFB-Pokal|1993]]. The club finished runners-up across three competitions in 2002, including the [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]]. After over 30 years without silverware, the club won their [[2023–24 Bundesliga|first Bundesliga title]] and their second [[2023–24 DFB-Pokal|DFB Pokal]] in 2024,{{Cite web |url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/bayer-leverkusen-are-2023-24-bundesliga-champions-26930 |title=Bayer Leverkusen are 2023/24 Bundesliga champions! |website=bundesliga.com |publisher=Deutsche Fußball Liga |date=14 April 2024 |access-date=14 April 2024 |url-status=live |archive-date=14 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240414175118/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/bayer-leverkusen-are-2023-24-bundesliga-champions-26930}}{{cite web |url=http://www.bayer04.de/b04-eng/en/_site_index.aspx |title=Bayer 04 Honours |work=Bayer Leverkusen |access-date=9 October 2014 |archive-date=27 September 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927150152/http://www.bayer04.de/b04-eng/en/_site_index.aspx |url-status=live }} becoming the first German team to win the league or [[Double (association football)|domestic double]] [[List of unbeaten football club seasons#Europe|unbeaten]], while setting the [[European association football club records and statistics#Longest unbeaten run across all competitions|European record for consecutive unbeaten competitive games]] (51)."}}
